object: doubly robust (Neyman-orthogonal) estimation of a functional under missing-not-at-random labels
claim: 2411.02771 (abstract + conclusion, per card): calibrated debiased machine learning estimates linear functionals of a regression function with double robustness of asymptotic normality under an asymptotic partial-orthogonality condition; isotonic calibration of the outcome regression and of the Riesz-representer (propensity-type) nuisance gives root-n, learner-agnostic confidence intervals via a bootstrap. 2608.11475 (abstract + open_questions, per card): linear-probe precision/F1 scored against sparse SwissProt annotations are explicitly 'lower bounds' because model-correct predictions on unannotated residues are charged as false positives, and the paper names formalizing this missing-label correction 'e.g. as positive-unlabeled learning' as an open question. Shared object: the influence-function / Riesz-representer correction for a functional (probe precision = P(probe correct | probe predicts positive)) estimated when the label-observed indicator is missing not at random.
asymmetry: Stats has a learner-agnostic estimator that is doubly robust for inference (valid CIs when only the annotation-propensity model OR only the label regression converges fast enough) plus a few-line isotonic implementation; compbio currently publishes an uncorrected, downward-biased lower bound and lists the correction as unsolved. Compbio contributes a concrete high-dimensional test bed (per-residue probe scores contrasted across the Pairformer trunk and the diffusion module) that exercises the 'one nuisance inconsistent' regime the stats paper validates only on semi-synthetic benchmarks.
must_be_true: Probe 'decodability' can be written as a linear functional of the regression function P(true label | activation) -- e.g. probe precision or true-positive rate.

The SwissProt annotation process is modelable as a missingness mechanism with overlap (every residue context has positive probability of being annotated), or a sensitivity/bounds model is substituted where overlap fails.
An asymptotic partial-orthogonality (mixed-bias) condition holds for that functional in the annotation-missingness model, so calibrating the two nuisances suffices for valid inference.
A subset of residues carries dense gold labels (DSSP-style) usable to fit the annotation-propensity nuisance.

object: Neyman-orthogonal estimation of an intervention effect with a high-dimensional nuisance control (omitted-variable / partialling-out correction)
claim: 2411.02771 (abstract + conclusion, per card): DML / one-step estimation orthogonalizes the target parameter against high-dimensional nuisances (outcome regression plus Riesz representer), giving root-n inference on causal / incremental effects with black-box controls, and calibration keeps this valid when one nuisance is inconsistent. 2608.11475 (abstract + limitations, per card): a strand-direction steering vector with probe F1 = 0.82 produces no measurable dose-dependent change in predicted structure, but the card flags this null as confounded -- interventions modify only the trunk single representation s and never the pair representation z, and 'strand information may live in z'. Shared object: estimation of the causal effect of a representation-space intervention while partialling out a high-dimensional correlated control (z).
asymmetry: Compbio has the gold-standard manipulation (direct do-intervention with matched-norm random controls and a dose-response readout) but no way to adjust for the z confounder and no confidence intervals on steering effect sizes; stats has orthogonal-moment estimators that stay valid with z as a high-dimensional nuisance and need only one nuisance well estimated. Conversely the compbio setting removes the positivity/overlap problem DML normally carries, because the 'treatment' is a direction the analyst sets exactly.
must_be_true: The pair representation z, or a sufficient low-dimensional summary of it, is observable and usable as a control covariate for the effect of the s-space direction on predicted secondary-structure content.
The linear-representation hypothesis holds well enough that 'the strand direction' is a stable target whose incremental (dose) effect is a well-defined estimand.
The map from (s, z) to predicted structure admits a Neyman-orthogonal moment for the direction's incremental effect (a partial-orthogonality condition).
Matched-norm random directions are an adequate stand-in for the no-intervention counterfactual at each dose.
